utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You've had a good rest yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything was all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Morrissey: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Tirak. Mr. Tirak, yesterday I commenced to ask you some questions about orders that you got from Rasim Delic at a senior level to conduct particular operations. I'm going to come back to a list of those documents in minute, but I just wanted to ask you one thing before I go to that. In late August and early September of 1993, you became aware that an inspection team had been appointed to come down to Herzegovina and help the 6th Corps coordinate combat action that it had to undertake; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I was aware, the inspection team visited the 6th Corps, but that was a lot earlier. I wasn't there myself. I'm not sure whether another visit was announced for late October or early September. As I wasn't there, I simply don't know. I believe I've stated this on a number of occasions already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, let me ask you, then. In the month of July, do you recall meeting any of Mr. Suljevic, Karic, or Bilajac, coming to Herzegovina to assist the 6th Corps in coordinating its -- its activities with the 4th Corps on the one flank and the 3rd Corps on the other flank?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that. It was sometime around mid-summer, but I can't be very specific. Those three gentlemen came to the 6th Corps. I met them, and we familiarised them with our situation. Then proceeded to tell us about the situation in the adjacent course so that we would keep ourselves mutually informed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Now, yesterday I showed you a document, D105, which was an order from Commander Delic early in July. When I say to you, I mean to the command of the 6th Corps. Now I want to look at another document, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And if the witness could be shown another exhibit, please, which has already been tendered, D138.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's about to be shown to you on the television screen is an order by Sefer Halilovic in his capacity as Chief of Staff dated the 24th of August and directed to the 6th Corps. Now, that should appear on the screen in front of you in just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have some difficulties with the English version, but B/C/S is on there. So could we proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour. I'll just see if I have a hard copy myself to proceed from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could I ask, Mr. Tirak, do you have in front of you a B/C/S version of that document? That is, an order of the 24th of August, 1993, under the hand of Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see part of the document. I can't see the entire document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, we think there is a technical hitch. Pardon me again, Mr. Tirak, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, we think the Bosnian that's on the screen is Mr. Delic's order of the 26th, not Mr. Halilovic's order of the 24th. I'm going to come to that order of the 26th soon, but I think we'd better show the witness the right one. Sorry. Just excuse me, Your Honour. I'll see if I've -- if we've caused the problem or --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's rectified now, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. It's been indicated that it's now rectified.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'm sorry. Do you have the Bosnian version of an order from Sefer Halilovic in front of you which is dated the 24th of August, 1993, and directed to the command of the 6th Corps and also to the command of the 4th Corps for information? Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, do you see at the end of that document that Halilovic has issued this order in his capacity as the Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see the bottom of the document, but I assume that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. I just want to show that to you because -- Mr. Tirak, I'm going to show you a number of documents. If there's a part that you need to see, you don't wait for me to give you permission. You just say so, and the court staff will assist you by scrolling to that point?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So could the witness just be shown the end of that order, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I see it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So now that appears to be to be an order by Sefer Halilovic in his capacity as Chief of Staff. And I take it since you were a Chief of Staff yourself, you're able to say this that a Chief of Staff can issue a combat order so long as his commander gives them the authority to do so; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite correct. This was the rule, that the Chief of Staff could only issue an order that has previously about authorised by the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in your experience, it did happen to you from -- not in this particular concrete case, but in other cases when you were Chief of Staff that sometimes you were given authority to issue a particular combat order on a case-by-case basis. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. Throughout my time as Chief of Staff, it only happened once that there was an emergency. Igman was attacked, and I was the only one around who had the powers to issue an order, but normally I didn't do this sort of thing. This was an exceptional situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Thank you. Well, as to the substance of that order, you can see now, and perhaps if we go back to the first page as well, you can see there that the Chief of Staff, Sefer Halilovic, issued a number of pretty detailed instructions to the 6th Corps as to what they should do to deal with the particular crisis at that time. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, as a matter of -- of reaction by the 6th Corps, did the 6th Corps form any plans to obey that order?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I don't think I can answer that question. We're obviously talking about a point in time when I'd left already, and I'm not familiar with any details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think I'd better just clarify that. This document's dated the 24th of August, 1993. When you say you'd left already, do you mean that you had gone to some other part of the front line or some other part of the area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point in time, in late summer, we were facing a great deal of difficulty in the Fojnica area. I spent the best part of my time on that patch because we were facing a great deal of difficulty. The HVO forces were attempting to cut our only line of communication over to Zenica and the 3rd Corps, which was the reason I spent the best part of my time in the area. Whenever I returned to the corps, it would be openly for a brief while, and I didn't have any time to do anything else with the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Would you just look at the map that's positioned behind you above your right shoulder.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I wonder if the witness could please be given a pointer to assist him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, does that map include Fojnica or not?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would need to stand up, if I may, to have a look.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, feel free. Mr. Tirak, if it doesn't appear there, I won't trouble you any further. I'm sorry, I should have checked it myself to see whether it did. Can you just indicate -- perhaps I'll ask you another question about it. We might deal with it in another way. Where is Fojnica in relation to the city of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In relation to the city of Konjic, Fojnica would be to the east -- the north-east rather.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: North-east. Okay. And about how many kilometres north-east was it?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you take the usual road, maybe 30 or 40 kilometres. At the time, however, you had to take the long way round, through the woods, which made it a lot longer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what was the normal travel time between Fojnica and Konjic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're lucky, 14 or 15 hours, but it could take a long longer than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. Well, now, I was going to ask you, and in fact I started to ask you what it was that the 6th Corps did in response to this order, but your answer to me seems to be this: That you had gone to Fojnica and you don't know what they did in response to that order; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent the best part of the time in that sector of our corps' area of responsibility, so I'm not familiar with details, but I suppose you would need to go ask those who were at the staff at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. I want to show you another -- another order, and this is one two days later from Commander Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown D139 now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's going to be put on the screen is another order somewhat similar in nature but emanating from a different person, from Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have some technical problem that we cannot have the English version of that document. Maybe you could proceed and later on this problem will be solved.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, we can, but it's -- I was just trying -- Your Honours, I'll explain what my dilemma is. Just excuse me, sorry, Mr. Tirak. Your Honours, putting these orders in is not very entertaining, if I can use that term, for anyone, not the witness, not the Bench, not me, I dare say not the Prosecution either. It has to be done, Your Honour, in a way which preserves some chronology, otherwise we're going to be lost in a whole load of orders, and I can indicate quite plainly -- what I'm meaning to do is to put such documents as I have in -- essentially in chronological order so that the Tribunal gets some use from it, frankly. And it's also unfair to the witness in some ways to jump from one to another because they forget -- well, sometimes witnesses forget what they're being asked and that's why I wanted to do it in the order that I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, could I just consult briefly with Mr. -- with my helpers here and see if I can find a way of doing it from paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What I mean is maybe we could proceed based on the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I'm happy to do that but I'm not sure if the Prosecutors' have got a copy of the document. I think I have. I was come up on the screen. But I'm -- I'm happy to proceed that way, Your Honour, if the Prosecutors are. Your Honour, we could put the English versions on the ELMO, which might assist everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Our legal assistant is just going to get unmarked ones. The ones that are marked at the moment might not be proper to put on the ELMO, I'm sorry to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tirak, just excuse us, please, while we attempt to bring technology under control. Just while we're waiting for the English version to be collected, would you take the opportunity, please, just to read the Bosnian version of the order that appears on the screen there, and just note who it's sent by and also the date on which it's sent, and then I'll ask you some questions about it when the English version arrives.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I find the Defence has become very dependent on the E-court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps while we're waiting Mr. Tirak, I'll get you -- okay.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps you can ask me some other questions. I don't think it will cause any confusion if we go back to this at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, thanks for the suggestion, but I think just to preserve some coherence for the rest of us in Court --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have an English version of this, and perhaps that could be placed on the ELMO now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just having regard to that document on the ELMO, could I just ask that -- do you confirm that that appears to be a document dated the 26th of August, 1993, addressed to the 6th Corps commander in person and emanating from the commander of the army, Rasim Delic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document states precisely that in no uncertain terms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could I just ask the document be moved down so the instructions under the heading "Order" can be shown. So I'm grateful for that. Okay. Now, do you observe here that Commander Delic asked your commend E, that is to say commander Gusic, to engage in an attack. Look at paragraph number 1. "To engage in an attack on the Vrdi village." Domazet village access. Do you see that? It's under paragraph 1 of that order.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you also see that in paragraph number 4 there's an order to ask the 44th and 45th Mountain Brigades to engage the HVO as closely as possible with the objective of tying down those forces and, if possible, to achieve success there. Do you see that part?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now I'll just ask you to have another look at that map, if you wouldn't mind. Do you see at the -- and I'm -- ask you to look particularly down towards the bottom of the -- of the combat line there. Are you able to see Vrdi, the village of Vrdi?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And does it appear to you that on that map it seems to indicate that there should be an attack towards Vrdi?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, based on what I can see on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And looking on that map a little bit higher up, a little bit further to the north, does it also appear to you that that map indicates that there should be attacks in the areas of the 44th and 45th Mountain Brigades, according to that map?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to come back to that map a little later on, but in short, do you agree that the attacks which Commander Delic has asked for -- to happen on the 26th of August do appear to have taken place or at least -- sorry, I take that back. The attacks requested by Commander Delic in this order of the 26th do appear to have formed part of the attacks depicted on that map that you've just looked at; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: By all means. That's what the map shows, offensive operations being carried out in an area that is a lot larger than that pertaining to those two brigades only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's certainly correct. Very well. Thank you for that. Now, because there was an order from Commander Delic to the 6th Corps command, I want to ask you questions about what the 6th Corps command did to put that order into practice, and my first question is: Were you present at the 6th Corps command at that time or were you engaged in other duties in the Fojnica area?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said before, I spent most of my time in the area, but being familiar with the situation as it was in the 6th Corps, I believe these orders were a little unrealistic. If anything, the corps situation did not allow for this. What Commander Gusic did about it, or did anything, I can't say. What I can say is we weren't able to do much. The corps simply wasn't able to at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but as to the specific response to that order, you were not in a position to make any comment one way or the other. Is that accurate? 23

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's accurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And -- all right, well, I'll just move on to another document straight away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown another document, and this is D140, already tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tirak, I'm now going to show you another document. Actually, while I'm waiting for that to come up, I'm going to ask you another question. The two orders I've just shown you, the one from Sefer Halilovic as Chief of Staff on the 24th and the other one from Delic on the 26th, have you ever seen those orders before today?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it when you were at Fojnica there was no requirement for Commander Gusic or his deputy, Bahrudin Fazlic, to forward such orders on to you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no such orders were conveyed to me. They probably believed the difficulty I was facing in my area was quite sufficient and that I should not be dealing with anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And to the best of your memory, they didn't -- neither -- neither Gusic nor Fazlic told us about these orders at the time as far as you can recall?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Thank you. Now, do you have now in front of you -- I'm just not sure what the technical situation is -- pardon me. All right. In front of you now there should be a document which is a proposal. Do you see that document, the proposal?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still have the old document on my screen. Well, yes, I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm just going to have to ask the court staff for some acrobatic assistance with this document. I just want -- what I want to do is show you the front -- the front page and ask you some questions. Then I want to show you the last page to get signature, and then I'll ask you about the substance of it. So, first of all, does this appear to be a proposal directed to the 6th Corps command, personally to the commander, dated at Jablanica 29th of August, 1993, and it is a proposal for planning and carrying out combat operations. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the beginning of the document but not the end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to give you a chance to -- to look at the document properly so -- and if you need more time you just don't -- don't wait for me to offer you say that you need more time. However, I just want to get some formalities first?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown the very end of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm seeking to show you now is the -- the name of the author of that document, which we think is a person called Mr. Zukanovic, and I'll just ask you to look at that. Okay. Do you have that now?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall Mr. Zukanovic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is unclear. I -- I mean, I do remember the name, but I don't have a clear memory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. In any event, seeing that, that signature there, a member of the ON OG operations and training, main command, Enes Zukanovic. Do you agree that he was a person who was located in that particular branch of the 6th Corps?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a while he was a member of the 6th Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if -- perhaps if we could just go back to the first page. Mr. Tirak, I'm going to take you through this proposal by Zukanovic to the commander of the 6th Corps. Okay. Could we just start by noticing the introductory paragraph, and could I just ask you to -- to note there that this proposal appears to be based on information gathered by and in the zone of the 44th, the 45th Mountain Brigades, and also the Prozor Independent Battalion, and contemplates a coordinated action by those groups? Do you agree that that's what the -- what the proposal appears to be based on?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, having regard to the specific of the proposal, I just want to take you through those. Do you see that paragraph 1 provides for particular axes of attacks by those units, the Prozor Independent Battalion and the 45th and 44th brigades?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And in particular, would you just have regard to the heading under the Prozor Independent Battalion, that one of the axes of attack there appears to be the village of Scip -- I'm sorry, I can't pronounce that one. But Scipe, Uzdol, and another village?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kranjcici, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And does the proposal go on, and do you have paragraph 2 in front of you there which is headed "Time of carrying out operations?"

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the English version that's on the second page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so far as you're aware, in early September there was some combat in the Konjic area which essentially involved a battle on the 2nd of September, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that much earlier a smaller operation had been planned in order to try and, so to say, do away with a pocket of resistance of the HVO members who after having been defeated in that particular theatre of war had joined the units of the Republika Srpska and engaged in coordinated activity around Konjic. So we had planned a relatively small action in order to remove them from that area in order to make for a safer communication between Konjic and Jablanica. And that plan had been devised a lot earlier but, because of ongoing problems within the corps, probably it had only been possible to start working on it at that stage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. Very well. Now, just having regard to the map that's next to you there, this is a map that was drafted at a later time, but I just want to -- I want to -- want to clarify a couple of things about this proposal by Zukanovic and the map that appears there. As you see that Zukanovic proposed certain attacks for the Prozor Independent Battalion in the area of Uzdol, do you know there that the Prozor independent -- you notice there that the -- that the Prozor Independent -- sorry, do you notice there -- I'll withdraw that. I'll deal with -- I'll deal with that when I come to the map. Pardon me. I don't want -- I don't want to overdo that. Very well. Just to press on with the Zukanovic document, would you look at number 4, paragraph 4, please, under the heading "Engagement of forces." Do you have that in front of you? And if not, tell us and we'll have it scrolled down for you. All right. Now, having had the opportunity to look at that and the particular axis of engagement of those units, I understand that map there is on a very large scale and includes more units than just the Prozor Battalion and the 44th and the 45th, but do you agree with this, that the proposals of Mr. Zukanovic, on -- in this document here that you're looking, at appear to be similar in nature to the attacks that are proposed on that map that's in front of you there?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: At any rate, very similar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now I must ask you a question about the Zukanovic document. Before I showed it to you here in court today, have you ever seen it before?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's in evidence in this case. I just want you to think back. Did the Prosecutors show you that document in their proofing session before you gave evidence here?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many documents did they show you in those proofing sessions?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very little about those preparations, because I have explicitly stated that at the time I was not there, and so all I can say is what I heard from Fazlic's -- Fazlic, the deputy commander. So I was not shown any actual documents myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. All right. Well, with respect to this plan of Zukanovic, did you hear about it at the time when -- when he made this proposal?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, when the learned Prosecutor Mr. Sachdeva asked you questions about whether the 6th Corps had engaged in any planning activities concerning combat operations in the area, you indicated the 6th Corps hand engage in any such planning. But let me ask you this question: Is the real truth about that, that you weren't aware of any such planning but, in fact, you were over at Fojnica and you don't really know?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly couldn't have known, but normally within the corps even when much smaller actions were about to be carried out, the first programming stage, the entire staff would be present. So that was the custom. And when I said yesterday the command of the 6th Corps did not actually device a plan for such an action, this is something that I can still say, as to whether an individual had ever made a proposal in relation to such an action and in what way. But the established custom was that at the start of the planning for any action, everybody would participate. Well, that was not adhered to this time round, and if anyone within the 6th Corps had been planning it, I was not aware of it, and that's why I stated explicitly yesterday that the 6th Corps Staff that -- was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, is your position really this: You weren't told the 6th Corps command was involved. In the normal course of events, if things were normal, you should have been told if they were, but at the time, things weren't normal and you were stuck over in Fojnica. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: So your suggestion would be along the lines of my answer, had you asked me a direct question, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll always try to ask you a better question, but I'm putting to you that you over at Fojnica did not know whether or not the 6th Corps was participating. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'm going to ask you about some particular dates, and you just do the best you can to answer. You think you were over at Fojnica before those orders that I showed you earlier on, the Sefer Halilovic order of the 24th of August and the Delic order of the 26th of August. Can you remember what date it was that you first went over to Fojnica during this particular stay at Fojnica that you've referred to? Was it mid-August or was it about the 20th of August? Give us your best estimate, please.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was the case even before, because throughout the month of August quite often different types of operations were conducted around Fojnica, because the HVO was trying very hard to cut of the communication line, the only one that we still had. So I think it might have happened before. I think it did, but I can't remember exactly. Whatever date I gave you would be approximate, because I just don't have such a specific and precise memory after 12 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, and, Mr. Tirak, we're not going to quarrel with you over that. That's quite reasonable. Bearing in mind the concerns that you've just expressed, do you think it was early in August that you went over there?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very difficult to give a precise answer, but I think yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, now, I'm going to really ask you about some dates towards the end of August, and you understand I have to put these to you formally and in an organised way. On the 30th of August of 1993, the likelihood is that you were over in Fojnica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know -- I'm going to ask you about the 1st of September. On the 1st of September, were you in Konjic when Sefer Halilovic and Sefko Hodzic -- sorry, in Jablanica when Sefko Hodzic and Sefer Halilovic arrived, or were you over in Fojnica?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was either at Fojnica or Vakuf or travelling between the two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Were you present -- so I take it you weren't present at any meeting between Sefer Halilovic, Zuka, being Zulfikar Alispago, Selmo Cikotic, and Salko Gusic on the 1st of September? You weren't present at any such meeting, is that true?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you were told of any such meeting or given any notes of any such meeting on 1st of September, at the time?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told about that meeting by Mr. Fazlic without any notes being taken. Just a couple of things in relation to that meeting were mentioned in a conversation. That happened when I came back from Vakuf that night, as I mentioned before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the night when you came back and learned that some crimes had been committed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to come to that night in some detail later on, but I want to go through the days before that just to make sure we're clear where you were and what you heard or what you didn't hear. I've asked you about the 1st of September. I want to come to the 2nd of September. On the 2nd of September, were you at or near to Konjic when combat activity was going on, and Sefer Halilovic, Zulfikar Alispago, and another individual named Haso Hakalovic were present and had a discussion? Were you present on that occasion at Konjic or were you over at Fojnica again?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't at Fojnica at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Where were you on that occasion, this being the 2nd of September?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very difficult to tell with any degree of precision. I've told you before, if you keep insisting on specific dates, I'm unable to answer. What I mentioned several times before, and I'm going to mention it again, is I don't really remember the date, but at the time of that operation I was either at Fojnica or at Vakuf, and you can ask me as many times as you like about the exact date, but my answer is always going to stay the same because I just simply cannot recollect the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tirak, I hear your answer. I understand what you say, but at the same time we've got a chronology to deal with in this case, and I have to persist with these questions. You just bear with me, please, and I'll come to the 3rd of September now. Were you aware on that day that Sefer Halilovic -- were you present on that day when Sefer Halilovic and the journalist Sefko Hodzic came to Kostanic -- Kostajnica and interviewed on tape some refugees who were -- and camp inmates who were placed there, or were you elsewhere at Fojnica, Vakuf, or halfway between?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't at Kostajnica at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And where you were is in one of the three positions that you've indicated, either Vakuf, Fojnica, or on the road in between; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I was in that particular area. And as to when, on what day I was in any specific place, I can't tell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. It may be that some. Indents I mention help your memory. It may be they don't. But I'm going to mention them and give you the chance. I take you to the 4th of September, were you present on the 4th of September when Commander Delic came down to Herzegovina and held a meeting at Jablanica with Sefer Halilovic and a variety of other persons including certain local commanders?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I just want you to have a look at that map there next to you. Do you see that -- just -- yes. Take your time to position yourself so you can see it. Does that map appear to you to be, as a matter of form, a map depicting a particular operation with the name of Neretva?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Undoubtedly that's what it says on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And now as a matter of military form, do you see in the top left-hand corner that that document has been approved with the word "Odobravan" by the commander, Commander Delic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you see in the bottom right-hand corner it's been countersigned by the Chief of Staff, Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and one can see that clearly as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just as a matter of form, based on that map, that would lead you to the conclusion that Commander Delic was the commander of the operation, and Sefer Halilovic was the Chief of Staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: At any rate, Delic signed that operation, so he must have been formally a commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Commander Delic didn't tell you anything about that map when you saw him a week later at Visoko, did he?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, when you saw him up at Visoko, he was pretending that he knew nothing about it; correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, yes, that he knew roughly, but he didn't know any details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. And -- yes, very well. Thanks. Had you ever been shown -- have you ever been shown that map before this courtroom today?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And on the 4th of September, you were not present. I think you've already indicated this. You were not present at this meeting at Jablanica when the map was signed. Were you told about that map at the time it was signed, namely on or around the 4th of September?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you just explain what the communications were like between the 6th Corps headquarters at Konjic and your base of operations out at Fojnica when you were there?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those communications were pretty bad. And when there was something urgent or something special had to be done, I used to go from Fojnica to Visoko, and from there we could have a securer communication with Fojnica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I understand. Was -- well, I'll come to the communications in a general way later on, so I wasn't ask you bits and pieces of questions about it. Thank you for your answers about that. I want to move on to the 5th of September. I asked you yesterday this question, but I have to just put it again because it -- to -- in order to preserve the chronology. On the 5th of September, you were not at Dobro Polje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn that there was a meeting at Dobro Polje at which Sefer Halilovic explained how the specific axes of the operation were to be carried out to the junior commanders?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not present at that meeting, so I don't know exactly what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. Was the first -- sorry. So in terms of what contribution was made by -- by Fazlic or by Gusic at that meeting, you just can't comment because you weren't there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you spoke later on to Braco Fazlic, did he even mention that there'd been a meeting at Dobro Polje? I mean this -- the meeting with Fazlic before you went off to see Commander Delic.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that conversation, he mentioned the meeting at Jablanica. And as to a meeting at Dobro Polje, he never mentioned it. For what reason, I don't know. Perhaps he thought it was enough for him to tell me about Jablanica. Perhaps it was about similar things or exactly the same, I don't know, but he never mentioned it to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. Well, I'm not asking you really the question as to why he might have mentioned it or not mentioned it, but you've confirmed that in fact he didn't mention it and that's what my question was. Now, on the 5th of September, did you become aware as to whether or not the 6th Corps had undertaken to collect troops from Sarajevo who were going to pass through the tunnel and come down to Herzegovina for combat operations? Did you receive any news about that where you were?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I'll move quickly through the dates of the 6th -- 6th and 7th of September, and I come to those two dates now. On those two dates, 6 and 7th of September, I take it that you were performing the same function that you've indicated all along. Namely, you were either at Fojnica, or Vakuf, or travelling between the two. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I come to the 8th of September. Were you aware that Bakir Alispahic, the minister of the interior of the Bosnian Republic, was present at Jablanica on that date?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that later, but I was not aware of it at the time, simply because I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. How much later did you hear that? Was that in October or was that during your conversation with Mr. Fazlic later on?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not during my conversation with Mr. Fazlic. It was a little later. Fazlic did not refer to that particular detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it sometime after you came back from Visoko to visit Commander Delic that you heard this information about -- about Bakir Alispahic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some days after my return from Visoko, I can't say how many exactly; that's when I found out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you found out, who was it who told you?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember specifically who was the first to tell me. I know that I asked Commander Gusic what Mr. Alispahic had been looking for, but I received no answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, on the 8th of September, positioned where you were, did you become aware, did you learn that units from Sarajevo were coming to Herzegovina, and in particular I'm referring to elements of the 2nd Independent Battalion, also elements of the 9th Brigade, and also elements of the 10th Brigade. Did you become aware on the 8th that such units were coming down, in fact were en route from Hrasnica and the tunnel down to Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 9th of September -- now, we've heard in evidence this case that the killings took place on the 8th, the night of the 8th of September, and the morning of the 9th of September, and I now turn to ask you questions about the 9th of September. On the 9th of September, did you speak a man called Zajko Sihirlic who was a security officer in the 44th Jablanica Brigade, part of the 6th Corps?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to an individual called Sead Kurt who was chief the Military Police Battalion -- sorry, I've glorified it there, the Military Police Company in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's -- there's a document I want to show you and ask you whether you saw it at the time and indeed whether you've ever seen it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And could the witness please be shown Exhibit D153.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's being brought up on the screen now, Mr. Tirak, is a document signed by Mr. Sihirlic reporting certain operative information that he had. I just want to give you the chance to look at it. Do you have in front of you a document dated the 9th of September, 1993, emanating from Zajko Sihirlic and also signed by Fadil Kevric? Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I just want you to read that -- that -- just -- just if you would quickly.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you scroll on, please. Can you scroll down, please. Further down, please. I've finished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. Do you know, or did you know at the time Mr. Zajko Sihirlic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I met him, but I think I only met him once or twice, tops. I would be hard put to recognise him now, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That's okay. I won't -- you won't be asked to, Mr. Tirak. But as far as you know, he was -- he was in the SVB, and he had to report up the professional line of reporting to Mr. Nermin Eminovic rather than the Command Staff generally. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Turning to that report then, can I ask you when this report was send to the 6th Corps command military security sector, did that report ever get shown to you at that time?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Inaudible]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I suppose that Mr. Fazlic saw this document. When I saw him that evening, I told me that there were indications that someone had been mistreated there, but he couldn't see anything more specific. I left straight away, but I assume that was the only document that Mr. Fazlic had seen by that time, and I believe he based his statement to me on that document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Have you seen that document in subsequent times?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I saw the report drafted by the assistant commander for security of the 6th Corps, and that was a little later. But he probably had that document, too, in his possession. I believe he based his report on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to come to the substance of these discussions in just a moment. What I want to do before I go any further is just to fix a general chronology of what you did in the next few days after this.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, did you come back to Konjic after being in the field at Fojnica, Vakuf, and in between on the 9th or the 10th or the 11th of September, 1993? Can you recall which of those days or, if it's another day, which other day, you returned to Konjic and spoke to Braco Fazlic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really sorry, but I really can't be very specific about the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. Well, I rather suspected that that would be the case. And what I want to do is take you to some incidents and see if we can build up a chronology that's reliable just based on your memory. Can you say what time of day you got back to Konjic, approximately? Was it evening? Or was it morning? Was it lunchtime? When was it?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, late in the evening. I can't be more specific. It was night-time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. All right. You arrived at Konjic at night-time. How long did you stay at Konjic speaking to your deputy and then to Mr. Fazlic before you set off to go to Visoko? Again, giving your best estimate.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's really difficult to be accurate. I spoke to my deputy briefly. He informed me about what was going on. I wanted to learn as much as possible in as short a time as possible, so I went to see my deputy immediately. I spoke to him for some time. It's difficult to say how long. I know that I only had several hours' time left to sleep and that I had to head back immediately. It was probably late at night already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you set off, did you go to Visoko early the next morning? In other words, did you stop and have some sleep or did you leave straight away?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I slept for several hours and then I set out. I remember this clearly, and the reason is we had some problems. I tried to rush it, but it took almost one day and one night to reach Visoko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. So is this accurate then: You came back to Konjic at night. You had a sleep -- sorry, you had your meetings, then you had a sleep, and then you set off again the next morning, and you came to Konjic after -- you came to Visoko after about 24 hours? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you arrive at Visoko in the morning?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Properly speaking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have booked in a meeting with Commander Delic already? In other words, were you expected?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And how long did you have to wait before you got an audience with Commander Delic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not very long. At the time I arrived, I didn't have the impression that there were too many people around at the command. That's as far as you could actually term that school building a command. I knew that that was the place to find him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And did you go directly there and speak to Commander Delic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've indicated that you spoke to him for a number of hours. Did that conversation start straight away?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when that conversation finished, approximately what time of the day was it? I don't expect an exact hour, but was it afternoon, evening, lunchtime?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's really hard to say exactly, but I do know that the whole thing went on for several hours. It must have been around lunchtime, I guess. But this is not something that is lodged in my memory. Therefore, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters' note, would the witness please be asked not to cover his mouth when speaking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tirak, the interpreters have asked that you not cover your mouth with your hand when you're answering questions. I'm just passing that message on. In fact, what I do is cover the microphone with a piece of paper, so we all have our faults in that regard. Meanwhile, did you stay at Visoko that night or did you leave straight away and make your way back to the zone of the 6th Corps?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I was in the area, I decided to go to Zenica to see if it was possible to get some fuel for Fojnica from the ironworks in Zenica. We had run out of fuel entirely, and we needed some very badly. Therefore, I went straight to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And was that on the same day that you had seen Commander Delic? In other words, did you finish with Commander Delic and then go over to Zenica, or was that the following day?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the same day. The road between Visoko and Zenica could be travelled at the time, and it took up to half an hour perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you stay that night in Zenica or did you go back to Fojnica?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was very exhausted, so I spent the night in Zenica, and it wasn't until the next day that I actually got to speak to the people at the ironworks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So that -- the day following your interview with Commander Delic you were in Zenica with the ironworks people. During that day, did you finish your business in Zenica and go back to Fojnica, or did you stay in Zenica for longer?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were given a full tanker of fuel at Zenica. I joined the driver on the way back to Fojnica. That was the fastest way to go back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you got back to Fojnica did you resume your duties in Fojnica and stay there for a number of days?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember specifically. I stayed for a day or two but not longer. I had had this conversation with Mr. Delic that had nothing whatsoever to do with this operation, but it was on account of that that I was in a hurry to go back in order to get a headstart with some other things that needed doing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Well, we'll come to -- perhaps I should ask you this: When you're referring to these other things, are they things of a military nature that you're talking about, other military tasks that you had?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: All tasks were military tasks at the time, weren't they.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we'll come to those in a minute. But, however, you weren't present in Dobro Polje or in Voljevac or in any of the northern villages of the 6th Corps zone when combat operations began on the 13th of September; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think you made it quite clear you had nothing to do with those combat operations yourself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, I have to come back now to the Delic conversation. I think -- thank you for persisting with getting that chronology sorted out, but I think from what you say you were away from -- away from -- or -- sorry. Perhaps I've gotten into a tangle there. It took you a day to get to Visoko. Then you spent another day -- it took you a day and night to get to Visoko, another day and night to spend time with Delic and go to Zenica, and then on the third day you got some petrol and you got the tanker back to Fojnica. Is that an accurate, general summary of what you did?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I understand it's rough, and thank you for indicating that. Now I want to turn to the conversation that you had with Mr. Fazlic when you first came to Konjic after your time in the field, Fojnica, Vakuf, and elsewhere. In relation to the conversation you had with Mr. Fazlic, you indicated that Mr. Fazlic was saying that he'd played no part in the planning of this -- of this operation. Is that accurate? Is that what he was telling you?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He told me he attended the meeting at Jablanica and that later on based on what he'd heard at the meeting, he had issued appropriate orders to three units from the 6th Corps that had actually been involved with the operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say so -- and did he say which meeting that was? That was the meeting at -- at Jablanica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that the commander and he had arrived in Jablanica, that a forward command post had been set up there with some members from the Supreme Command Staff and Mr. Sefer Halilovic. A meeting was held there, he said, where a plan was tabled to lift the blockade of Mostar. There was a request for these three units from the 6th Corps to take part in that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what Mr. Fazlic was telling you at this time, according to you, was that he had already issued appropriate orders to those units resubordinating them. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said he had issued the relevant orders. I'm not sure what specific terms he used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But these orders had been issued, according to what he told you, already; in other words, he'd already done that by the time he was talking to you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what he told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And he then told you about certain -- well, perhaps I've just go -- to step outside the conversation you had with Mr. Fazlic and ask you some questions. Did you know that the -- a battalion called the Sutjeska Battalion took part in these combat operations that began on the 13th of September?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that the Prozor Independent Battalion took part in those operations?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he -- and did you know that will elements of the 44th brigade took part in that operation -- sorry in those combat actions?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you know that parts of the 45th brigade took part in that combat action?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that the 317th Brigade took part in that action?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did no one advise you in the days before you came to Konjic after the -- after the -- well, when you did come there, did no one advise you as Chief of Staff of the 6th Corps that these units were going to take part in combat operations prior to speaking to Mr. Fazlic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you certain that Mr. Fazlic mentioned the Prozor Independent Battalion in that conversation?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that the Independent Battalion would certainly be part of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just excuse me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Could I just deal with one question because it connects with this matter and then we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make a statement to the ICTY investigators in this case, in particular an individual named Mr. Bernard Brun, and did you say in that statement, which has been given to us by the Prosecutors, at paragraph 13, I'll just read it to you and get you to comment: "Only after the war I heard about the crime allegedly committed by Prozor Independent Battalion. At the time of operation I did not even know that this battalion was taking part in it." Now, did you tell that to the investigators, and if so, why?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know at the time of the operation. I told you when I found out, but the operation had already finished by this time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. So you could be wrong, then, in saying that Mr. Fazlic mentioned that the Prozor Independent Battalion was going to take part in the combat actions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic mentioned this to me. I'm not sure how exactly I put it to the investigators, but what I meant to say and what really is relevant is that I didn't know at the time of the operation. By the time Fazlic actually told me, I believe the operation had already been over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the time you spoke to Mr. Fazlic, in other words, as far as you understood it, there had already been combat activities take place, and in particular, the fighting at Uzdol had already taken place. Is that what you say?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My understanding of what Mr. Fazlic said, which is not necessarily accurate, it's very difficult for me to recall every single detail, so this at least was my understanding. Maybe these were not the precise words he used, but that was my understanding of the words he used. He said the operations surrounding the blocking of Mostar had already reached an end, had been brought to a conclusion. That was my understanding. I'm not sure if he was referring to some of the operations or the whole thing, the entire operation, so I can't be specific about that. One thing you must know, I kept no notes there for now. It's 12 years now. It's difficult to think back and remember every single detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the final question is your impression was that some of the combat had already commenced and in fact had already finished based on what Fazlic was telling you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on my understanding, and I may have been wrong. But my impression was that the operation was nearing an end. I may have been wrong about it, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That might be the appropriate time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes we will take a longer break, and we will resume at quarter to five.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that the initial appearance went smoothly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I hope so, Your Honour, but it's completed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That's what I mean. And how long do you think you could use for the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I find it difficult to say at the moment, Your Honour, because there are documents being put to the witness, but I can indicate that I will finish him today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Of course. I hope we could have some time to discuss, you know, the issue we discussed yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe at least an hour? Because we have two hours to go, and in between we will have a short break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll do everything I can. But however, Your Honours, you will have observed on occasion I'm told to slow down, as well, by the interpreters. Anyway, I shall do my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much, Mr. Tirak. Now, I was asking you questions about the conversation that you've narrated with Mr. Fazlic and I now want to turn to the information he was able to give to you about crimes. At the time that he spoke to you, it appeared to you -- he was able to say simply that there had been mistreatment of civilians in Grabovica, but he was unable to give you any information beyond that. Is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And perhaps to come to the point, was he actually able to tell you whether there had even been any murders at that stage? Did he have that specific information to give you or was he limited simply to mistreatment?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing specific. He mentioned nothing specific. When I asked him whether he had any specific details, he said, "Well, all I know at the moment is that there was some ill-treatment and problems there," but he couldn't say anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So at that time, your information came really from Mr. Fazlic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And therefore at that time you didn't have any information about who the perpetrators of these -- of this mistreatment might have been; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact, you didn't have any information as to whether the perpetrators were, all of them, military people or whether some of them might have been refugees. Is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, I only had that piece of information and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I understand. Okay. And so were you -- before you met with Mr. Fazlic, were you planning to go to Visoko to see Rasim Delic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point, certainly not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was according to an order given to you by Mr. Fazlic as acting commander that you went to Visoko; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that conversation and after his order, of course I decided to go to Visoko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I understand. But the -- the trigger, if you like, for you going to Visoko was to tell Delic news of this mistreatment of civilians. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not just that but many other things as well, and especially Fazlic's order was aimed at units from Sarajevo, and more specifically the 9th and the 10th to be withdrawn immediately from that territory, because his assessment was that they could only cause problems and that in terms of an offensive they would not be of any great use. That was his order that I was asked to relay to Mr. Delic to withdraw these units immediately back to Sarajevo. And as to crimes, he said to mention what he knew -- that is to say what I knew as well. So I only said that we received information about some ill-treatment having taken place there, but I had no clear indication of what sort of ill-treatment and who the perpetrators were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. I understand that. Now, apart from those instructions that Mr. Fazlic gave you as to what you should tell Mr. Delic, did he tell you anything else that you should relay to Mr. Delic or was that the extent of his instructions to you?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some other matters in conjunction with a somewhat unclear situation as to who was in command of the 317th Brigade. Some were claiming that it was up to the 3rd Corps and then the 6th Corps and then the 3rd once again. And then I put a question to Mr. Delic, and I asked him to give me a clear definition and to issue clear orders as to who would be in command there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But can I ask you, was that one of the things that Bahrudin Fazlic asked you to raise or is that something you raised on your own motion later?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was what Bahrudin Fazlic said. And apart from that, I also brought up a whole range of issues and made comments which have nothing to do with this operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. I won't -- once you saw Mr. Delic, obviously you had other things to talk about with him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well -- but nevertheless, we'll just stick with the ones that concern this case. Now, given the limited information that you had about the mistreatment of civilians, did you make any contact with Nermin Eminovic who was head of the 6th Corps security to find out more? Before you went to Visoko, I mean.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, certainly not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make any contact with Vehbija Karic to find out about this mistreatment?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That evening, I only talked to the deputy Andric and the one from Visoko. If we think of contacts with usual people at the staff, I mean asking them to bring me coffee or something else. But in military terms, I only talked to those two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. I understand you say you didn't contact any else. I just have to put these names to you to be sure that you didn't contact these people. You didn't contact Sefer Halilovic that evening, did you?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attempt -- did you contact or attempt to contact Zulfikar Alispago?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attempt to contact the local police in Jablanica, Ermin Zubic, or his or his deputy Ahmed Salihamidzic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to Sead Kurt of the military police in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to Zajko Sihirlic of the SVB in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Bahrudin Fazlic tell you that he'd spoken to any of these individuals?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: What he said, of course, I can't remember exactly, but he said he had just received the report from Jablanica to the fact that in the area of Grabovica some mistreatment had taken place and I didn't ask anything else and he didn't tell me who he heard it from. Probably he got some reports from the field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. My final question about that is did he tell you whether it came from the -- from the military or that it came from the civilian police or the MUP, that information?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He just said that he got those reports from Jablanica. He didn't specify who he heard it from. Perhaps he did, but I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm now going to turn to the meeting with Mr. -- with Commander Delic. Just excuse me one moment. Okay. Could the witness please be shown D157 again. This is the order that purports to be from Commander Delic. I'm just going to show you that order that you were shown yesterday, which is dated the 12th of the 9th apparently, and under the hand of Commander Rasim Delic. Do you have that in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The 12th of September according to the terminology of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. Did I say the 12th of August? I apologise. Yes, the 12th of September. Very well. Now, just looking at that order there, I just want you to notice the preamble in the paragraph commencing: "The 6th Corps Chief of Staff has informed me about the decision of the chief of the Supreme Command Staff regarding planned combat operations towards Prozor and Mostar." Now, you see -- you see that section there?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And in respect of that, was there a specific decision of the chief of the Supreme Command to which you referred Commander Delic in reality?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As to whether such a decision existed, I don't know, but I did not comment the decision of the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command. I simply relayed to him what commander Fazlic told me, but I never commented on that decision. As to whether Mr. Delic was aware of that decision and as to whether he made a comment, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And as far as any decision of the supreme -- of the chief of the Supreme Command Staff, you gave Delic no information about any such decision; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I simply told him, as I've mentioned over and over again, what I heard from Mr. Fazlic, no more, no less, for as long as we're talking about this situation. As for other topics we had much broader conversations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. I understand that. Just given your experience as Chief of Staff, what's the difference in military terminology between a decision and an order?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no big difference, no essential difference, but an order is something you don't question, and you have to carry it out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's a decision?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Basically the same in military terms. That's the way I interpret it. That's it's a somewhat softer version but consequences are the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Well, a decision is the sort of instruction that -- that the head of an inspection team -- sorry, the decisions are the sort of instruction that a Chief of Staff might give when explaining and emphasising the commands of a commander; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, but in the sense of the duty or the obligation to carry out, it's the same. That's what I had in mind when I said earlier on that they both had similar consequences.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that, but in -- take a situation -- I'll put a hypothetical to you. Take a situation where you as Chief of Staff had to explain an order that had been issued by your commander to some junior troops. In that situation, you would be entitled to issue a decision explaining and clarifying what the commander meant; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereas if you were the commander as such, you would just issue a straight-out order; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Thanks. Very well. Now, there's a reference in the second paragraph of this order here, on this document, I should call it, which refers to genocide by members of the 1st Corps, 9th Mountain Brigade. Now, you didn't give Delic any such information, did you?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I've already said it before. I've already told you what I've told him, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tirak, I apologise, but just because of the nature of this case there are some times I have to put something to you in a particular order even though you have answered it in many respects before.
